the RNase A mechanism is a triester A + D associative mechanism with an internal H transfer to the O1P and that the general acid/base mechanism is not supported.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the triester mechanism is supported by our QM/MM simulations and the dianionic mechanism is supported by the crystallographic structures.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the RNase A mechanism is not a simple one-step reaction, but rather a two-step mechanism with the first step (cleavage-transesterificaton) being the slowest step in the catalytic cycle.
